vjimc-2017-cat1-01.prompt:
Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function satisfying
$$f(x+2y)=2f(x)f(y)$$
for every $x,y\in\mathbb R$. Prove that $f$ is constant.
vjimc-2017-cat1-01.answer: $y=0$ gives $f\equiv0$ or $f(0)=\frac12$. In the second case $x=0$ gives $f(2y)=f(y)$, so $f(a)=f(a/2^n)\to f(0)=\frac12$.

vjimc-2017-cat1-02.prompt:
We say that we extend a finite sequence of positive integers $(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ if we replace it by
$$(1,2,\dots,a_1-1,a_1,1,2,\dots,a_2-1,a_2,1,2,\dots,a_3-1,a_3,\dots,1,2,\dots,a_n-1,a_n),$$
i.e., each element $k$ of the original sequence is replaced by $1,2,\dots,k-1,k$. Géza takes the sequence $(1,2,\dots,9)$ and he extends it $2017$ times. Then he chooses randomly one element of the resulting sequence. What is the probability that the chosen element is $1$?

vjimc-2017-cat1-03.prompt: Let $P$ be a convex polyhedron. Jaroslav writes a non-negative real number to every vertex of $P$ in such a way that the sum of these numbers is $1$. Afterwards, to every edge he writes the product of the numbers at the two endpoints of that edge. Prove that the sum of the numbers at the edges is at most $\frac38$.
vjimc-2017-cat1-03.answer: Some maximizer is supported on a clique of the (planar) edge graph, hence on at most $4$ vertices, and $\sum_{i<j\le4}a_ia_j\le\frac38$ when $\sum a_i=1$.

vjimc-2017-cat1-04.prompt:
Let $f\colon(1,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a continuously differentiable function satisfying $f(x)\le x^2\log(x)$ and $f'(x)>0$ for every $x\in(1,\infty)$. Prove that
$$\int_1^\infty\frac1{f'(x)}\,dx=\infty .$$
vjimc-2017-cat1-04.answer: Cauchy–Schwarz: $\big(\int_e^a\frac1{f'}\big)\big(\int_e^a\frac{f'}{(x\log x)^2}\big)\ge(\log\log a)^2$. Integration by parts with $f\le x^2\log x$ gives $\int_e^a\frac{f'}{(x\log x)^2}\le2\log\log a+C$.
